explanation: Humans have a pair fewer than chimpanzees, gorillas and orangutans, because 2 ancestral ape chromosomes fused end to end to form human chromosome 2.

claims.text: Chimpanzees have 48 chromosomes in each body cell, in 24 pairs.
Humans have 46 chromosomes in each body cell, in 23 pairs.
Gorillas and orangutans also have 48 chromosomes.
Human chromosome 2 formed from the end-to-end fusion of 2 ancestral chromosomes that remain separate in other great apes.

writerNotes: Self-check (guide 9.3), all eleven codes confirmed true. The selfCheck field itself is left out because the CNT-1 item schema refuses it as an unknown key, so the codes are recorded here. lint: content:check reports no errors and no warnings for this item. claims: four listed, all high because each holds a number. One search on great ape chromosome numbers and the chromosome 2 fusion should cover them. datasets: no pinned dataset in content/datasets/manifest.json covers animal or plant biology, so none applies and every high-risk claim needs web evidence from checker A. rivalTest: 'humans must have more' is the planted trap. Exact counts, so the guard allows a gap of 2. Argued against the key: 48 for chimpanzees and 46 for humans are standard figures, and body cells excludes eggs and sperm. volatility: evergreen, a settled fact that cannot change; no time words, and nothing rests on knowledge newer than mid-2026. regional: a global fact. style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, explanation of 24 words. myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches; the explanation speaks of shared ancestral chromosomes, never of humans descending from chimpanzees, so it stays clear of the humans-from-chimpanzees entry. mystery and encore: nothing of either kind in a comparison item. doubts: none. Classed as Nature because it is about apes and evolution, though genetics borders on Science & Tech.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Human chromosome 2 is the product of two ancestral ape chromosomes joining. Researchers believe the two original chromosomes fused end to end, and human chromosome 2 was derived from two smaller chromosomes that are found in other great apes (now called 2A and 2B). Fluorescence in-situ hybridization (FISH) work confirmed that two ancestral Great Ape chromosomes fused at their telomeric repeats to form the HSA2.
